headline: NHL trade board 2.0: Expanding the list to 20 top targets after a big week of moves
take:
The Athletic's updated trade board puts Dylan Larkin at the top of its list of 20 targets, coming after the Connor Hellebuyck trade. As The Hockey News' Mike Fink posted, the Devils notebook this week covers "Dylan Larkin opens up his trade list."

Our numbers say the Red Wings captain is playing better than his stat line shows. Larkin has two goals and six points in 10 games so far this season, but his own expected goals (the quality of his shot chances) come to 3.03, about one goal more than he has scored. At 5-on-5 Detroit has generated 56.3% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share runs 2.58 percentage points better with him than without. He's playing 21.69 minutes a night, and our model has him at 1.08 expected goals per 60. That's a small sample, but the process points to a scorer who is due, not one in decline, after a 34-goal, 67-point season last year. For a buyer, that means paying for a top-line center whose results should catch up to his chances. For fantasy owners, it's a reason to hold if he's available.
